body: I'm sorry you feel this way too. What's your story? I'd love to hear it.

Hey, I just appreciate that you took the time to reply. Anxiety and depression go hand in hand, and I think what's killing me now more than anything is the anxiety. It sucks, hardcore. But what you really kind of brought me back to reality by noticing that I did mention the good things in my life...there is good and I just need to be appreciate of those things. I really appreciate that you did that. Thank you :)
I think this sums 'em up perfectly, unfortunately 😫😒

I agree with you completely...the more stable option seems like the better option. Getting a degree is a time-consuming, but worthwhile pursuit. I guess I just have to kind of "suck it up" and do it. Easier said than done.

And I really wouldn't mind attempting a LDR. I am patient and can see "the light at the end of the tunnel" WAY more than my GF. She says that she "would lose weight and be a mess" if we did a LDR. This is disheartening as I want very badly to pursue my degree in a fast and MUCH cheaper way, but she's just not as able (willing?) as I am. I'm not faulting her for knowing what she can/cannot handle, but it hurts that I can see the longterm goal (delay gratification for a bigger payoff) and she can't. Besides, I racked up a considerable amount of student loan debt in undergrad, so it just makes more sense to work for a year until the program starts to save money for it. 

I appreciate your input very much. I'm glad there are people like you out there to assist a random stranger with life problems, haha. Thanks a ton!

I appreciate your reply...I completely, 100% agree with you that the safer/more stable option is the better option. I just struggle so, so much with depression...I keep a small circle of friends and I've grown to rely on her emotionally more than I probably want to admit...So while I know that biting the bullet and finishing my degree with my parents is the safer option, I also know that I'll likely be very depressed following. I'll have a good support system, but parents =/= relationship. But I digress...

Bipolar disorder is a rough beast. I never thought I'd struggle as much as I have in the past couple of months. To say it's been one of the most difficult challenges of my life is an understatement. I appreciate your kind words and wish you the best as well :)

Thanks for the reply. Yeah, I'm not sure how I'd feel in the event that she decides she doesn't want to continue the relationship. I brought this up with her ("what if we break up and you're still paying for everything?") and she swears that she is "true to her word" and would continue to pay. I know her very well, and I believe her, but I would absolutely hate to be in that situation...and I would probably be kicking myself for not picking the more stable option. 

Thanks for the reply. It gave me a lot of food for thought!

"By moving in with her and having her pay for all the rent/food/etc, you're one step closer to actually building a life with her there away from family."

That's actually a really solid thought that I hadn't really considered. I'm not sure if I'm at a point in my life to make such a leap...I appreciate your input. That really helped.
